asr.full_text: The fallout continues for Wells Fargo. Top banking analyst Mike Mayo of CLSA releasing a note saying. His firm's previously strong support for Wells Fargo CEO John Stumpf is now wavering. Mayo calls. Stumpf's response to the recent crisis reactionary versus leading. He writes, Wells Fargo is bigger. Than a CEO, notwithstanding a good financial track record during his tenure, there should be no more. Excuses for the lack of answers to key questions. The note details five issues that CLSA believes. Wells Fargo needs to address. First, how long the problems could continue for. Second, what Wells is. Doing to help impacted customers. Third, the note calls for clawbacks to be put in place in terms of. Pay. Fourth, Mayo says Stumpf should voluntarily reduce his own compensation. And fifth, the analyst. Argues Wells needs to restructure its board and possibly split the chair role from the CEO. Mayo, though, still rates the stock as an outperform with a $57 price target. Of course, for Wells this. Week, the focus very much is going to be on Thursday's House hearing following the Senate. Hearing last week, and Mayer basically suggests that this is his last chance for the CEO to. Perform, whereas going into last week's, he needed a lot more to happen to lose his position. He now says this is a must-win kind of performance from Stump in order to hold onto his position. To watch the latest from CNBC. Thanks for watching.
